Skip to content

Skills and Projects: Consolidation and Cleanup Plan

Built from the Oct 15, 2026 audit (skills-and-projects-audit.html): 257 skills, 52 project folders. Phase 1 is done (Oct 15 and 16). Every other step below is still a proposal for your approval. Revised Oct 15 after reading how DashComm Pro and its Remote Workers load skills.

  • Goal and rules
  • Verify first
  • DashComm
  • Phase 1: safe removals
  • Phase 2: diverged copies
  • Phase 3: project to personal
  • Phase 4: personal pruning
  • Phase 5: project hygiene
  • Phase 6: distribute skills
  • Keeping it clean
  • Decisions for you

Goal and where each skill should live

257 → about 210skills after Phases 1 to 3 (about 190 if you also approve Phase 4 archiving)
24 → 6copies of the 6 Stripe skills (18 are redundant worktree copies)
9 → 0skills that exist in two places with different contents
9 → 0projects sitting on main or master instead of dev

One rule decides where a skill belongs: how many places will you need it?

Placement rules
Skill kindLives inWhy
Used from more than one project or from anywhere (inbox cleanup, logo creation, email setup, security audit, MVP builder)Account skills (the Synced folder inside each DashComm account folder), with a copy in Personal (~/.claude/skills) as the git-backed sourceDashComm tabs read the account folder, not ~/.claude/skills (see the DashComm section below). The Personal folder is still the one backed up to GitHub (claude-skills-backup), so it is the source of truth that gets copied out.
Your own skills that other tools or devices also need (inbox, weekly brief, documents)Account skills (Synced)Follows your account. This is what this app actually loaded in today's session. Each account folder has its own set, so a skill must be placed in every account that needs it.
Only makes sense inside one project (Darktide build capture, map rasterizer, Stripe skills in FerretBooks)Project (.claude/skills in that project)Ships with the repo and stays out of every other session's list.
Knowledge-vault tooling (wiki-ingest, wiki-lint, canvas)Plugin (claude-obsidian), not copied into vaultsThe vault copies are byte-identical to the plugin copies, so every update has to be made twice.
Reference material that is not a procedure (the media-kits design references)A reference folder or SOP, not a skillIt has 43 attached files and mentions many projects. It is a library, not an action.

Verify first (before moving anything)

Which skill folders does each tool actually load? The DashComm section below explains why personal skills most likely do not load here. Run the test to confirm.
Original question: In today's session the skill list showed your account-synced skills (anthropic-skills:...), plugin skills and built-ins. It did not show the 105 skills in your personal folder, such as logo-creation or security-audit. The command-line version of Claude Code loads personal skills, but this app may not. If it does not, moving project skills to Personal would hide them here.
  1. In this app, open a new session in an unrelated folder and ask it to list its skills. Note whether security-audit (personal-only) appears.
  2. Repeat in the Claude Code command line.
  3. If personal skills do not load in this app, change the placement rule: use Synced for everything you need here, and keep Personal as the git-backed archive.

File dates in the audit are the dates files were written or synced, not necessarily when you last edited them. Every "newer" claim below needs a quick diff before deleting the older copy.

How DashComm and Remote Workers change this plan

Read from DashComm Pro (README, src/main/updatePolicy.ts, docs/sops/orchestrator.md, docs/sops/remote-control.md) and your account folders. Item 1 is inferred from the docs and this session's skill list, and is not yet tested.

What DashComm does and what it means here
#FactEffect on the plan
1Each DashComm tab runs Claude with its own account config folder and user-level settings only. It does not read ~/.claude/skills, the root .claude/skills, or a project's CLAUDE.md. This session listed only synced, plugin and built-in skills."Convert to Personal" does not make a skill work in DashComm. The target is the account skills folder. Personal stays as the git-backed source that gets copied out.
2You have 13 account folders. Only 4 hold skills, with about 9, 10, 19 and 20 each. The other 9 hold none.Tabs on 9 accounts have no custom skills. The sets have drifted. Phase 6 gives every account the same approved set.
3A Remote Worker is a second computer running DashComm. It uses its own Claude folders. DashComm does not copy global instructions or skills to it, and standing rules and the second-opinion tool do not work on worker tabs.Any skill you rely on must also be installed on each worker. Phase 6 includes a worker step. Do not assume a worker tab follows your CLAUDE.md rules.
4DashComm's updater pulls from a pinned branch, default dev. It refuses if the folder is not on that branch, if origin changed, or if the new tip does not build on the current commit. DashComm's default branch is dev, and pushing to it publishes nothing until you sign a release.Your keep-it-on-dev rule is what DashComm itself depends on. Leave DashComm Pro out of the "make dev equal main" work. Never rewrite or force-push its dev.
5DashComm creates its own worktrees (.claude/worktrees inside projects and the DashComm-*-wt folders). Its cleanup refuses when a worktree has uncommitted work.Worktree removal in Phases 1 and 5 goes through git worktree remove after checking that no open tab or Parallel Run uses the folder. Never delete the folders by hand.

Phase 1: Safe removals (low risk, high clutter win)

These are copies or placeholders. Archive to a dated folder instead of deleting, so git history and the folder both keep them.

Phase 1 status: done, except the ADA worktree. Everything was moved, not deleted, to Brandon's Apps\.claude\_archive\2026-10\quick-wins\. That folder is git-ignored, so it is not backed up by git.
  • 1.1 The two old FerretBooks agent worktrees are archived. Left in place on purpose: ADA Worktrees\FerretBooks (branch ada-fixes, 3 unpushed commits and 1 uncommitted file). The archived reconciled-mark-order tree holds uncommitted work and 1 unmerged commit, so review it before emptying the archive.
  • 1.2 The 15 duplicate skills are gone from the Property Llama vault. The separate git clone under Property Llama Workspace\PL Work Folder still has them.
  • 1.3 template-skill removed and committed in the personal skills repo (commit 320918f).
  • 1.4 The WardenKey copy of self-updating-local-app is archived; the personal copy is now committed. In WardenKey the file shows as a deleted, uncommitted change on master.
  • 1.5, 1.6 The root transcript-to-notion-tasks and InboxHelm messages-cleanup copies are archived. The messages-cleanup copies differed only by a trailing newline.
Phase 1 actions
#ActionSkills affectedRisk
1.1Remove the Stripe skill copies that sit inside throwaway worktrees: FerretBooks\.claude\worktrees\agent-a3100b846d8eae5cc, FerretBooks\.claude\worktrees\reconciled-mark-order, and the whole ADA Worktrees\FerretBooks folder once its branch is merged. Do it with git worktree remove, not by deleting folders, and first confirm no open DashComm tab or Parallel Run uses the folder.18 duplicate skills (connect-recommend, stripe-best-practices, stripe-directory, stripe-docs, stripe-projects, upgrade-stripe × 3)Low check each worktree has no unmerged work first
1.2Delete the vault copies of skills that are identical to the claude-obsidian plugin: autoresearch, canvas, defuddle, obsidian-bases, obsidian-markdown, save, think, wiki, wiki-cli, wiki-fold, wiki-ingest, wiki-lint, wiki-mode, wiki-query, wiki-retrieve. Keep the three Property Llama ones (see 3.6).15 skills in the Property Llama vaultLow-Medium confirm the plugin is enabled when Claude runs inside the vault
1.3Remove template-skill, a 7-line placeholder ("Replace with description of the skill...").1 skillNone
1.4Remove the project copy of self-updating-local-app in WardenKey. It is identical to the personal copy.1 skillLow
1.5Remove the root copy of transcript-to-notion-tasks. It is identical to the synced copy. Separately decide whether to retire the skill, since you now put tasks in ScopeTask, not Notion (see Decisions).1 skillLow
1.6Remove the project copy of messages-cleanup in InboxHelm. It differs from the synced copy by one line.1 skillLow look at the one differing line first

Phase 2: Resolve the nine skills that exist twice with different contents

For each pair: diff, merge anything worth keeping into the winner, archive the loser. "Diff size" is the number of changed lines.

Diverged pairs and recommendation
SkillCopy ACopy BDiff sizeRecommendation
docxPersonal, 197 lines, dated Jun 27Synced, 94 lines, dated Sep 29213Keep synced (the copy DashComm loads). Archive the personal copy (it looks like the older stock version).
pdfPersonal, 295 lines, Jun 27Synced, 315 lines, Sep 2236Keep synced. Small diff: skim it, then archive the personal copy.
pptxPersonal, 484 lines, Jun 27Synced, 271 lines, Oct 2735Keep synced. Archive personal after checking nothing of yours was added.
xlsxPersonal, 289 lines, Jun 27Synced, 100 lines, Sep 22355Keep synced. Archive personal.
skill-creatorPersonal, 210 lines, Jun 27Synced, 486 lines, Sep 22662Keep synced (more than twice as long, so it is the richer one). Archive personal.
clean-inboxPersonal, 199 lines, Oct 14Synced, 168 lines, Oct 14275Real merge needed. This is your most-used skill and both copies were edited the same day. Diff them, fold the extra rules into one, and keep that one in Synced. Update the SOP in SOPs.html to match.
weekly-briefRoot project, 526 lines, Sep 3Synced, 105 lines, Sep 22461Keep synced if the shorter version still produces the brief correctly. Run it once to confirm, then archive the root copy.
logo-creationPersonal, 125 lines, Sep 28Root project, 338 lines, Sep 30449The root one is bigger and newer. Merge into one, keep it in the account skills, and copy it to Personal. Check that your rule about archiving old logo versions survives the merge.
messages-cleanupSynced, 157 lines, Sep 22InboxHelm project, 158 lines, Sep 151Keep synced. Covered by step 1.6.

Phase 3: Project-level skills: convert, keep, or retire

Every project-level, commands-folder and vault skill that is not simply a duplicate.

Project-level skill decisions
#SkillNow inVerdictReason
3.1build-mvpRoot .claude/skillsMove to account skills (copy kept in Personal)A generic idea-to-deployed-MVP builder. The root folder only works when a session starts under Brandon's Apps.
3.2logo-creationRoot + PersonalMerge, keep in account skills + PersonalSee Phase 2. It is used by name across Fal.ai Bridge, Famtinerary, Tabor and ThriveMapper.
3.3squarespace-domain-consolidationRootMerge with squarespace-domain-migrate, keep in account skills + PersonalTwo skills for the same job, and the personal one has no description so it never triggers. Keep the better text under one name with a proper description.
3.4model-chat, multi-agent-chromeRoot .claude/CommandsConvert or retireOld command-style folders dated May 7 that predate your skills setup. If you still use them, move to Personal under skills/. If not, archive. Note: multi-agent-chrome runs several Chrome instances in parallel, which may clash with your "reuse one browser tab" rule.
3.5media-kitsRootReclassify, not a skillDescribed as a repository of design-system references with 43 files. Move it to a reference folder (or the SOPs folder) and leave a one-line skill pointing to it, or drop the skill wrapper.
3.6pl-inbox-updates, pl-meeting-followup, email-template-pipelineProperty Llama vaultMove to account skills (keep pl- prefix; copy kept in Personal)You run Property Llama work from your personal workspace, not only from inside the vault, so vault-only skills do not trigger where you need them. Rename email-template-pipeline to pl-email-template-pipeline.
3.7instructional-videoPersonal vaultMove to account skills (copy kept in Personal)A YouTube tutorial-video designer for your personal brand. It is not tied to the vault folder.
3.8upload-to-reconroomYouTube MCPKeep, or convertIts text names Darktide Archivum and ScreenLoop as well, so it is used across three projects. Move to account skills if you upload from outside YouTube MCP.
3.9gmail-inbox-triageInboxHelmRetireDrives Gmail in Chrome. Your standing rule is clean-inbox over the InboxHelm connector, never Chrome triage.
3.10capture-gameslantern-build, rasterize-mission-mapsDarktide ArchivumKeep in projectSpecific to that repo's data and scripts.
3.11Six Stripe skillsFerretBooks .agents/skillsKeep in project (one set)Installed from Stripe for FerretBooks only. If Tabor or ScopeTask billing also needs them, convert to Personal then.

Phase 4: Personal folder pruning (optional, measure first)

105 personal skills: 47 belong to gstack (third-party, excluded from your backup, leave alone) and 58 are yours or imported.

  • Imported generics dated Jun 27 were added in one batch and never edited. Candidates to archive if you do not use them: raffle-winner-picker, twitter-algorithm-optimizer, slack-gif-creator, skill-share, tailored-resume-generator, competitive-ads-extractor, langsmith-fetch, internal-comms, theme-factory, brand-guidelines, image-enhancer, youtube-downloader, developer-growth-analysis, meeting-insights-analyzer, lead-research-assistant, content-research-writer.
  • Overlapping pairs to merge or pick one: connect and connect-apps; email-setup, wire-up-integration, cloudflare-email-service and the synced resend-cloudflare-email-setup; domain-name-brainstormer and the synced domain-availability-check; file-organizer, invoice-organizer, downloads-cleanup and tax-doc-organizer; security-audit and app-audit (plus the built-in security-review).
  • Cloudflare family (cloudflare, wrangler, workers-best-practices, durable-objects, agents-sdk, sandbox-sdk, web-perf, turnstile-spin): keep. You deploy on Cloudflare and Railway.
  • How to measure usage before pruning: search your session transcripts for each skill name over the last 90 days (I have not done this yet because it means scanning a lot of files; I can do it in small batches). Anything with zero uses goes to _archive/2026-10 inside the skills folder, not deleted.

Phase 5: Project hygiene

Project cleanup actions
#ActionProjectsNotes
5.1Status Oct 15: dev now matches main or master in 8 of the 9 projects. ScreenLoop's dev holds a merge of both lines (untested; master not yet moved). Folders are not switched yet. Switch back to dev (your rule: the source folder stays on dev; use a worktree for branch work).Automate With Brandon, Automated Options Trader, Darktide Archivum, Famtinerary, FunnelAnalyzer, LeadSifter, S2 Command, ScreenLoop, SoundControlProThis list excludes DashComm Pro, whose default branch is already dev. Check git status first. Darktide Archivum has 3 uncommitted changes. Do not switch a folder with uncommitted work until you decide what to do with it.
5.2Review uncommitted work.Active Listener Pro (23 changes, last commit Aug 25), Automate With Brandon (1), Darktide Archivum (3)Commit, stash or discard, one project at a time.
5.3Add a short CLAUDE.md (build/run commands, branch rule, links to the SOP).Darktide Archivum, Discord MCP, FakeReviewRadar, FunnelAnalyzer, InboxHelm, LeadSifter, ScreenLoop, SoundControlPro, Treadmill Gator, VideoTranscriber, WardenKey, YouTube MCPStart with InboxHelm, LeadSifter and WardenKey, the ones with active work.
5.4Add a GitHub remote (back up the code).ElevenLabs Bridge, Fuse at Park RowFuse at Park Row is a live investor site, so this one matters most.
5.5Prune finished worktrees at the root.Nine DashComm-*-wt folders, LeadSifter-enrichkey-wt, dcp-blank, dcp-global-instr, dcp-scratch-keepRun git worktree list in the parent repo. Remove only those whose branch is merged and that no open DashComm tab uses, with git worktree remove. These folders are DashComm-created.
5.6Decide the fate of non-repo folders.Cloudflare Sites, scopetask-migration, ADA WorktreesInitialize git, or archive if finished.

Phase 6: Distribute skills to every account and Remote Worker

New, because of how DashComm loads skills (see the DashComm section).

  1. Pick the approved set after Phases 2 to 4: one list of skills every account should have.
  2. Source of truth: the git-backed Personal folder (claude-skills-backup).
  3. Copy script: a small script copies the approved set into each account folder's skills folder, the same idea as DashComm's global-instructions feature, which copies CLAUDE.md into every account every 60 seconds. Start with the 4 accounts that already have skills, then add the others you actually use.
  4. Mark managed copies so a hand-edited skill inside an account is never overwritten (DashComm's CLAUDE.md copy uses a marker line for the same reason).
  5. Remote Workers: on each worker machine, clone the skills backup and run the same copy script. A worker tab still does not get your standing rules or second-opinion tool.
  6. Check: open a tab on each account and confirm the same skill list shows.

Open question: whether DashComm should do this copy itself, like its global-instructions feature. That would be a DashComm feature request, not part of this cleanup.

Keeping it clean afterwards

  1. One owner per skill. Add a column to SOPs.html naming each skill's home (Personal, Synced or Project). Your rule already says every new skill gets an SOP entry in the same session; this adds the location.
  2. Naming: prefix business-specific skills (pl- for Property Llama, ss- for Smart Syndicator) so a list sorts by business.
  3. Descriptions: every skill gets a trigger-rich description. Fix squarespace-domain-migrate first.
  4. Size: over 500 lines moves detail into reference files. Today only wrangler (923), slack-gif-creator (647) and the old weekly-brief (526) are over.
  5. Re-run the audit monthly. The generator is currently in a temp folder; move it to Scripts\ so it lasts. It is read-only and takes about 5 seconds.
  6. New skills: create in Personal, then run the copy script so every account and worker gets it.
  7. Never edit two copies. If a skill must exist in two places, one is a pointer to the other.

Decisions I need from you

  1. Confirm the test result: personal skills do not load in DashComm tabs. If they do, Phase 6 gets simpler.
  2. Which of the 13 accounts do you actually use? Those get the approved skill set.
  3. Do you use Remote Workers today, and on which machines?
  4. Is transcript-to-notion-tasks retired now that tasks go to ScopeTask, or should it be rewritten to target ScopeTask?
  5. Do you still use model-chat and multi-agent-chrome?
  6. May I archive the Jun 27 generic imports in Phase 4 if my usage check finds zero uses?
  7. Switch the 8 caught-up projects to dev now? ScreenLoop waits on your five uncommitted files.

Suggested order: Verify first, then Phase 1 (pure duplicates), then Phase 2, then Phase 3, then Phase 6 (distribute), then Phase 5. Phase 4 comes last and only after a usage check. Total effort is roughly a couple of hours of reviewed steps, and every deletion is an archive move with a git commit, so it can be undone.

Counts in this plan come from the audit's file scan. "Newer", "identical" and "unused" claims should be confirmed with a diff or usage search before each step.
